correctness.rationale: The target row is the first multiple of \(m\) above \(p\). Every selected index lies strictly between the low digit \(s\) and \(p\), forcing exactly one Kummer borrow, while every earlier admissible row is below \(p\) and has valuation zero. A separate leading-digit case split proves the global upper bound \(1\). Exact-integer replay checked 5,250 parameter pairs without contradiction.

value.rationale: The least extremal row is a named natural invariant introduced by the lead source. The result gives a complete exact classification of the entire first-valuation layer \(r_p(m)=1\), improves the known generic equality row from \(mp\) to a row less than \(p+m\), and identifies the exact valuation of every selected coefficient at the optimum. This is a structural infinite-family theorem rather than a routine finite computation.
